entities.name: Pledge
entities.short: A thing left with a pawnbroker as security for money lent: if the debt is not repaid on time, the thing stays with the lender. In the novel Raskolnikov pawns his things with the old pawnbroker Alyona Ivanovna.
entities.significance: The pledge is Raskolnikov’s way into the pawnbroker’s flat. In chapter 1 he brings her a silver watch and studies the rooms and the way she opens the door; in chapter 6 he prepares a false pledge, a piece of wood wrapped so tightly that it will take her time to untie it.

quotes.text: The pledge, however, was nothing but a smooth piece of wood planed to the size and thickness of a silver cigarette case.
quotes.interpretation: The false pledge is made for one purpose: to keep the pawnbroker busy with the knot for the moment Raskolnikov needs.
